title: A large language model-based approach to quantifying the effects of social determinants in liver transplant decisions

bias_targets.methodology: Extracting Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) from unstructured clinical notes using an LLM and applying Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition to quantify how much of the disparity in liver transplant listing rates across racial and ethnic groups is explained by these factors versus unexplained systemic differences.

Comparing the prevalence of various SDOH factors (such as lack of primary caregiver, trauma, and substance use) and liver transplant listing outcomes between male and female patients using statistical significance testing (two-proportion z-tests) and regression analysis.

Using an LLM to systematically extract socioeconomic indicators (e.g., housing instability, transportation barriers, insurance status, and social support) from psychosocial evaluation notes to measure their impact on clinical recommendations and predictive models for transplant listing.
